subject: Task 10.2 - Bounded, redacted log call sites and volume bounds (ADR-020 clauses 4 and 6)

findings.issue: docs/limitations.md SEC-5 still asserts the pre-10.2 negative claim that 'the plugin has no logging call sites, so no plugin log path can leak a secret' and 'the plugin still has no diagnostic log (ILogger/Serilog) call sites'. After task 10.2 this is false: 21 instrumented log call sites now exist. This is a stale false-assurance statement, not an exploitable defect; the new path is correctly documented in ADR-020, docs/architecture.md sections 6 and 12, and the worker report flags SEC-5 as stale. The plan assigns the SEC-5 rewrite to task 10.3.

findings.recommended_action: Complete the task 10.3 SEC-5 rewrite from the 'no logging call sites' negative result to the reviewed ADR-020 redaction contract before Gate 10. No code change is required for task 10.2.

findings.issue: The provider and metadata log call sites emit ArrProviderError.Message. ArrProviderError bounds the message to 512 chars but does not redact content, so the ADR-020 clause 4 guarantee for that field rests on every upstream producer. All current producers were enumerated and verified to use fixed, code-owned strings (no URL, key, header, or payload). This is a future-regression risk only, already acknowledged by the worker.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader.cs:85-89 and src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:178-186 (the only log sites that consume error.Message)
findings.recommended_action: Keep the producer-side invariant (fixed, code-owned ArrProviderError messages) covered by review; if a future provider-client change wants to surface response-derived text, add a redaction/sanitize step at ArrProviderError construction or before the log boundary. No action required for task 10.2.

findings.issue: Several log payload strings are length-bounded but not control-character-stripped: ArrProviderError.Message (trim/truncate), WorkProcessingResult.Reason (trim/truncate), and MediaMatch.AmbiguityReason (trim). ArtworkOperationErrors.Sanitize (used by artwork reasons) does strip control characters. Today every producer supplies fixed code-owned text, so no attacker-controlled value reaches these log lines and CR/LF log-forging is not exploitable. This is defense-in-depth only; it matters only if a future producer propagates response-derived text into one of these fields.
findings.recommended_action: Optional hardening: route log-bound reason strings through a control-character-stripping sanitizer at the boundary (the artwork path already does this) so a future producer cannot forge log lines. No action required for task 10.2.

findings.issue: docs/architecture.md section 12 prose lists 'durations' among the bounded values emitted by the logging boundary, but no 10.2 call site logs a duration. The section 12 limit row itself (Plugin log volume, 5 per minute per category/event, code-owned, suppression summary, 256-key cap) is accurate against LogThrottle's constants.
evidence: git diff HEAD -- src (no duration value appears in any of the 21 _log.Write payloads)
findings.recommended_action: Optional wording fix: drop 'durations' or add a duration-valued call site in a later task. The limit row is correct.

findings.issue: Every instrumented class takes an optional IArrTagsLog<T>? that defaults to null, so a non-DI construction that omits it emits nothing. This is a diagnostic gap (missing logs), not a secret-exposure path; production DI supplies the registered log for all boundaries (factories for ArtworkGenerationCoordinator and LibraryReconciliationService pass it explicitly, and the MVC TypeFilter construction path is covered by a test).
findings.recommended_action: None required; a future non-DI construction site should be required to pass the log.

summary: The task 10.2 logging path implements the ADR-020 clause 4 redaction contract and clause 6 volume bound correctly. All 21 instrumented log call sites were enumerated and each emits only bounded, already-redacted values (bounded enums/counts, Jellyfin item ids, the non-secret ArrConnectionId identity, configuration version, ArrProviderError code/retryability/fixed message, exception type names). No API key, webhook secret, SecretLease value, X-Api-Key/X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header, request/response body, provider DTO, or PluginConfiguration reaches a log line; no call site uses LogLevel.Trace or a level-conditional payload expansion, so raising verbosity to Debug/Trace cannot expand a redacted value (verified by the per-level sentinel theories and the Debug==Trace comparison). The LogThrottle is thread-safe and bounded (5 per category/event per minute, one suppression summary per window, 256-key cap; the tracking key is code-owned so the cap is effectively unreachable in production). DI wiring adds no custom ILoggerProvider/sink, does not replace the host ILoggerFactory, resolves ILogger<T> through the host DI with a NullLogger fallback, and yields ArrTags.* categories. The section 12 log-volume row is accurate. No BLOCKER, HIGH, or MEDIUM finding remains open. The only open finding is LOW documentation debt: docs/limitations.md SEC-5 still contains the stale 'no logging call sites' negative claim, which the plan explicitly assigns to task 10.3; the remaining findings are noted hardening/assurance observations. Verdict: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS.
